placements.purpose: The highlighted head/KV area is the concern this folder develops. Scoring, visibility, positional information and execution strategy remain separate questions about the same component. The map motivates the later GQA/MQA route; it is not evidence that those variants or a cache have already been implemented here.

placements.purpose: Follow the input into both projection branches, then keep the two resulting attention patterns distinct until their outputs are joined. Each general projection can use every input feature; this is not a requirement to divide the raw embedding into disjoint slices. Separate parameters allow different retrievals but do not guarantee linguistic specialization.

placements.section: Concatenation preserves the separate channels; projection mixes them
placements.purpose: Concatenation preserves the separate head channels; the following matrix can combine those channels into the layer’s output width. The output projection acts within a token row. It does not create a new attention distribution across tokens, and it is not required to mix every feature if the learned parameters preserve some channels.

placements.purpose: The packed matrix places the independent per-head projection columns together. Splitting its computed output recovers those head features without replacing the parameters with shared weights. This is why the equality below can be checked using one parameter set rather than comparing separately initialized layers.

placements.section: Transpose the right axes, then merge deliberately
placements.purpose: The transpose positions batch and head as the leading batch-like axes, leaving token and feature in the last two axes. Matrix multiplication can then compare tokens within one head. Reversing that transpose before merging is equally necessary: having the right number of elements does not establish the right token/head ordering.
